set_title: Sclerosis names: six different hardenings in brain, skin, spine, ducts and arteries
stem: A 40-year-old woman has had fingers that turn white and then blue in the cold for 3 years. Her fingertips have small ulcers, and the skin of her hands and face has become tight and shiny. She has heartburn and trouble swallowing solids. Anticentromere antibodies are positive.
oneliner: 40F + cold-induced white then blue fingers + tight shiny skin, heartburn, dysphagia + anticentromere antibodies → ?

whyNot.A: Tuberous sclerosis gives seizures and skin hamartomas; she has **tight skin and Raynaud**
whyNot.B: Monckeberg calcifies arteries; she has **tight skin and Raynaud**
whyNot.C: Multiple sclerosis causes neurologic relapses; she has **tight skin and esophageal dysmotility**
whyNot.D: ALS causes motor wasting; she has **Raynaud, tight skin and anticentromere antibodies**

why: Hardening of skin and organs from collagen deposition. **Raynaud, tight skin, esophageal dysmotility and anticentromere antibodies** is systemic sclerosis (limited form, CREST).

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Upper plus lower motor signs, sensation normal**

idea.rule: Raynaud + tight skin + dysphagia = systemic sclerosis; anticentromere = limited.
also: ACE inhibitors prevent scleroderma renal crisis

set_title: Glomerular disease names: membranous vs membranoproliferative and their neighbors
stem: A 45-year-old woman with chronic hepatitis C has edema, hematuria and blood pressure of 150/95 mm Hg. Urine protein is 4 g/day with red cells. C3 and C4 are low, cryoglobulins are present, and ANA is negative. A renal biopsy shows enlarged glomeruli with a double-contour appearance of the capillary walls on silver stain.
oneliner: 45F with hepatitis C + nephrotic range proteinuria with hematuria + low C3, C4 + tram-track basement membrane → ?

whyNot.A: Lupus nephritis needs lupus; she has **ANA negative, hepatitis C, cryoglobulins**
whyNot.B: Membranous disease has spike-and-dome deposits and no hematuria; hers has **tram-track GBM, hematuria**
whyNot.C: IgA nephropathy has normal complement; hers is **low C3 and C4 with hepatitis C**
whyNot.E: Poststreptococcal disease follows strep and clears; hers is **chronic with hepatitis C**

why: Thick membrane plus cell proliferation: mesangial cells wrap the capillary wall. **Tram-track basement membrane, hepatitis C and low C3** is membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis.

idea.rule: Nephrotic and nephritic together + tram-track GBM + low C3 = MPGN.
also: Hepatitis C or B, cryoglobulinemia, lupus

set_title: Poly- names: polycythemia, polymyositis, polymyalgia, polyarteritis, polycystic
stem: A 48-year-old woman cannot climb stairs or lift her arms to brush her hair after 3 months of progressive weakness. Muscles are not tender, strength is reduced in the hips and shoulders, and there is no rash. CK is 5,000 U/L. Anti-Jo-1 antibodies are positive. Biopsy shows CD8 T cells invading muscle fibers without perifascicular atrophy.
oneliner: 48F + 3 months of proximal weakness, no rash + CK 5,000 + anti-Jo-1 + CD8 T cells within muscle fibers → ?

whyNot.A: Polymyalgia has stiffness with normal CK; she has **weakness and CK 5,000**
whyNot.C: Polyarteritis nodosa is vasculitis with hypertension and neuropathy; she has **muscle inflammation, anti-Jo-1**
whyNot.D: Polycythemia vera is a blood disorder; she has **proximal weakness and high CK**
whyNot.E: Polycystic ovary syndrome is hormonal with irregular periods; she has **myopathy and anti-Jo-1**

why: Many muscles inflamed by cytotoxic T cells. **Proximal weakness, high CK, anti-Jo-1 and no rash** is polymyositis.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **High Hct, low EPO, JAK2; itch after shower**

idea.rule: Proximal weakness + high CK + no rash + CD8 T cells = polymyositis.
also: Anti-Jo-1 raises risk of interstitial lung disease

set_title: Poly- names: polycythemia, polymyositis, polymyalgia, polyarteritis, polycystic
stem: A 45-year-old man has had fever, weight loss, abdominal pain after meals, and testicular pain for 6 weeks. He has chronic hepatitis B. Blood pressure is 165/100 mm Hg. He has a right foot drop and tender skin nodules on the legs. Creatinine is raised, and ANCA is negative. Angiography shows aneurysms of renal arteries. His lungs are clear.
oneliner: 45M with hepatitis B + fever, post-meal abdominal pain, hypertension, foot drop + renal artery aneurysms + ANCA negative → ?

whyNot.A: Polycythemia vera has a high hematocrit; he has **fever, foot drop and arterial aneurysms**
whyNot.B: Polymyositis causes painless proximal weakness; he has **foot drop and renal aneurysms**
whyNot.C: Polymyalgia is stiffness in older women; he has **hypertension and visceral aneurysms**
whyNot.E: Polycystic ovary syndrome is a female hormone disorder; he has **hepatitis B and aneurysms**

why: Many arteries inflamed in nodules along medium vessels. **Hepatitis B, renal microaneurysms, hypertension and neuropathy with spared lungs** is polyarteritis nodosa.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **High Hct, low EPO, JAK2; itch after shower**

idea.rule: Hep B + medium-vessel vasculitis + renal aneurysms + lungs spared = PAN.
also: Beads on a string on angiography

set_title: Granulo- names: granuloma vs granulation tissue vs granulomatosis
stem: A 45-year-old man has had 2 months of nasal crusting, bloody nasal discharge and sinus pain. He now has cough with blood-streaked sputum. Urinalysis shows red cell casts, creatinine is 2.8 mg/dL, and chest x-ray shows multiple nodules. Cytoplasmic ANCA against proteinase 3 is positive.
oneliner: 45M + bloody nasal discharge, sinusitis, hemoptysis + RBC casts, high creatinine + lung nodules + c-ANCA (PR3) → ?

whyNot.A: EGPA has asthma, eosinophilia and p-ANCA; he has **sinus disease and c-ANCA**
whyNot.B: Granulation tissue is wound healing; he has **vasculitis with RBC casts**
whyNot.C: A granuloma is a lesion; he has **sinus, lung and kidney disease**
whyNot.D: Goodpasture spares sinuses and is ANCA-negative; he has **sinusitis, c-ANCA**

why: Granulomas plus small-vessel vasculitis in the sinus, lung and kidney. **Upper airway disease, hemoptysis, RBC casts and c-ANCA (PR3)** is granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

idea.rule: Sinus + lung + kidney + c-ANCA = granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

set_title: Granulo- names: granuloma vs granulation tissue vs granulomatosis
stem: A 40-year-old woman has had adult-onset asthma for 2 years and now has a left foot drop, numb fingers and purpuric leg lesions. Eosinophils are 20% of white cells. Perinuclear ANCA is positive. Chest x-ray shows transient patchy infiltrates. Nerve biopsy shows vasculitis with eosinophils.
oneliner: 40F + new asthma, foot drop, purpura + eosinophils 20% + p-ANCA + transient lung infiltrates → ?

whyNot.A: This vasculitis has sinus and kidney disease with c-ANCA; she has **asthma, eosinophilia, p-ANCA**
whyNot.B: CGD presents in childhood with infections; she has **asthma, eosinophilia and neuropathy**
whyNot.D: A granuloma is a tissue pattern; she has **systemic vasculitis with eosinophilia**
whyNot.E: Granulation tissue is wound repair; she has **eosinophilic vasculitis**

why: Eosinophils plus granulomatous vasculitis. **Asthma, eosinophilia, neuropathy and p-ANCA** is eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Churg-Strauss).

set_title: Granulo- names: granuloma vs granulation tissue vs granulomatosis
stem: A 3-year-old boy has had recurrent skin abscesses, a liver abscess and pneumonia from Staphylococcus aureus and Aspergillus. Nitroblue tetrazolium dye does not turn blue and the dihydrorhodamine test is abnormal. Lymph node biopsy shows granulomas. Immunoglobulins are normal. His maternal uncle had similar infections.
oneliner: 3M + recurrent S. aureus and Aspergillus abscesses + abnormal dihydrorhodamine test + granulomas + affected maternal uncle → ?

whyNot.A: A granuloma is a tissue pattern; he has **an inherited killing defect**
whyNot.C: Granulation tissue is wound repair; he has **recurrent catalase-positive infections**
whyNot.D: This vasculitis occurs in adults with asthma; he is **3 with abnormal DHR**
whyNot.E: This vasculitis occurs in adults; he is **3 with a failed respiratory burst**

why: Phagocytes cannot kill because NADPH oxidase is missing, so granulomas form. **Catalase-positive infections with an abnormal DHR test in a boy** is chronic granulomatous disease.

idea.rule: Catalase-positive infections + abnormal DHR/NBT = chronic granulomatous disease.

set_title: Pericarditis vs endocarditis names: which layer and what is growing on the valve
stem: A 28-year-old woman with a malar rash, arthralgia and positive anti-dsDNA antibodies has a new murmur. Three sets of blood cultures are negative. Echocardiography shows small warty growths on both the atrial and ventricular surfaces of the mitral valve.
oneliner: 28-year-old woman, SLE, negative cultures, growths on both sides of mitral valve → ?

whyNot.A: Usually fever with positive cultures; hers are **negative** with **SLE features**
whyNot.C: Occurs with cancer and clots on the closure line; she has **SLE features**
whyNot.D: Follows strep with Jones criteria; she has **malar rash and anti-dsDNA antibodies**
whyNot.E: Causes positional pain and ST elevation; she has **warty mitral valve growths**

why: Named for Libman and Sacks, who described sterile warty valve growths in lupus. **SLE with negative cultures and growths on both mitral surfaces** is typical.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Pain better leaning forward; diffuse ST elevation**
**Advanced cancer; sterile clots on closure line**
post-strep inflammation of all heart layers

idea.rule: Libman-Sacks = lupus, sterile, both valve surfaces. Marantic = cancer, sterile, closure line.
also: Verrucous growths on both valve surfaces

set_title: -ectasia words: something widened (telangiectasia, duct ectasia, lymphangiectasia)
stem: A 3-year-old boy has had an unsteady walk for a year and repeated sinus and lung infections. He has dilated red vessels on the whites of both eyes. Serum IgA is low.
oneliner: 3-year-old boy, unsteady gait + sinopulmonary infections + red conjunctival vessels + low IgA → ?

whyNot.B: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia brings nosebleeds and AVMs; he has **unsteady gait and low IgA**
whyNot.C: Mammary duct ectasia affects adult breasts; he is a **3-year-old boy**
whyNot.D: Intestinal lymphangiectasia causes edema and diarrhea, not **ataxia with low IgA**
whyNot.E: Bronchiectasis is airway widening; it does not explain the **unsteady gait and eye vessels**

why: Ataxia (incoordination) + telangiectasia (widened tiny vessels): an ATM DNA-repair defect. **Ataxia, eye telangiectasia and low IgA with sinopulmonary infections** fit.

idea.rule: Ataxia-telangiectasia: the name lists the two main signs.

set_title: Broncho- names: bronchiolitis, bronchiolitis obliterans, bronchopulmonary dysplasia and their look-alikes
stem: A 52-year-old man had a bilateral lung transplant 2 years ago for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Over 4 months he has had worsening shortness of breath on exertion and a dry cough, with no fever. His FEV1 has fallen 30% from its best value after the transplant, the FEV1/FVC ratio is low, and a bronchodilator does not change it. Expiratory CT images show patchy air trapping, and the airways are not dilated.
oneliner: 52M, lung transplant 2 years ago + slow dyspnea, falling FEV1 not reversed by bronchodilator + air trapping → ?

whyNot.A: Bronchiolitis strikes infants acutely; he is **52 with 4 months of slow decline**
whyNot.B: Bronchiectasis dilates airways with copious sputum; his **airways are not dilated**, cough dry
whyNot.D: Bronchogenic cyst is a single mediastinal mass; he has **patchy air trapping throughout**
whyNot.E: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia affects ventilated preterm newborns; he is **52, 2 years post-transplant**

why: Small airway inflammation + closing off: the bronchioles scar shut. **Fixed FEV1 fall with air trapping after lung transplant** is chronic rejection.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Infant's winter cold moving down to wheeze**
**Preterm, ventilated, still on oxygen at 36 weeks**
**Daily purulent sputum; airway wider than artery**

idea.rule: New fixed obstruction after lung or stem cell transplant = bronchiolitis obliterans.
also: Leading cause of late death after lung transplant
Also after GVHD, adenovirus, Mycoplasma or fumes
